summary: Compose a traversable island around a ridge, sheltered inlet and readable path.
objective: Build an island I can explore, with terrain-aware walkers and a clear route from jetty to lookout.
example_prompts: Build an island I can explore, with terrain-aware walkers and a clear route from jetty to lookout.

entities.name: Terrain
entities.guidance: Author silhouette before detail: ridge, saddle, shore shelf and cliff faces. Use rough rock, softer soil and low-gloss water as distinct material families; avoid uniform noise. Where a filled pond or stream is depicted, build a persistent base surface with a declared footprint and water level/profile distinct from the basin floor; add ripples or flow flecks as separate cues.

entities.name: Jetty and lookout
entities.guidance: Model posts into the support surface, deck thickness, rail joints and visible steps; inspect at walking distance.

entities.name: Walker
entities.guidance: Give feet, hips and a head a readable hierarchy; derive stride from traveled distance, plant feet against the support surface.

state_contract.model: Authored height field and static obstacles; controlled capsule actor with position, velocity and bounded steering acceleration in illustrative metres.
state_contract.authority: One canonical model owns semantic values; derive geometry and labels from it. Keep presentation transforms separate. If water is included, its level/profile and footprint own base coverage; the flow control and cue phase are separate presentation state.
actions: Select route waypoint; reject unreachable targets.
Pause or reset actor position and velocity.
Toggle terrain and obstacle collider overlay.

invariants: Collider includes body clearance; buildings and cliff walls block movement.
Sample support height and normal; enforce authored slope and step limits and block water unless swimming is implemented.
Bridge deck is a distinct support surface above water; do not sample seabed through it.

For a filled, non-draining authored water surface with unchanged level, hiding flow cues or setting authored flow to zero preserves base coverage; intentionally changing water volume or level needs a separate contract.
motion_guidance: Use fixed simulation steps, sweep capsule across movement and slide/stop at contact; interpolate rendering.
Constrain feet to terrain, limit heading change, and keep acceleration bounded in free motion; gravity only in unsupported states.
Animate optional flow cues over the persistent water surface. Pause freezes their state; reset restores declared water level/coverage and cue phase. No flow simulation is implied.
known_limits: Invented terrain, not a geologic or erosion model.
Navigation and contact implementation remain required; a waypoint curve alone does not establish clearance.
Authored guidance; no scene runtime or visual verification has run for this recipe.

object_craft.material: Rough cliff rock, softer matte soil, directional timber grain and a low-gloss water family; use contact darkening sparingly at supports.
object_craft.articulation: Parent feet to legs and legs to pelvis; heading follows resolved velocity, foot placement follows the selected support surface.

colliders: Capsule actor encompassing body; support contact handles feet.
Transformed static wall/roof bounds; terrain and bridge supports.
driving: Bound free-motion acceleration and turn rate; brake or replan at blocked route.
contact: Sweep movement, remove inward velocity, slide or stop.
Terrain normal, slope and step limits decide support; water is blocked.
physical_contract.timestep: Fixed simulation step with accumulated remainder; interpolate render transforms.
checks: Complete a route without penetration at declared tolerance.
Stop at shoreline and cliff; traverse bridge on its deck.
Pause and reset clear stale velocity.

If water is depicted, inspect overview and oblique shoreline/bridge views with flow cues hidden and with flow zero; intended wet regions stay covered and dry banks stay dry. Pause/reset preserves or restores declared coverage and cue state.

intent_signals: Keep a filled pond and stream surface visible while authored flow cues move or stop.
